full_judgment: 3. The defendant appeared in the suit and filed written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter alia, that the defendant used to live and work in United Kingdom and her husband Md Nurul Hadi gifted her 210 decimals of land vide registered gift deed No. 1799 dated 21-4-1990 and thereafter, the said Md. Nurul Hadi died leaving behind the defendant, son Ajmol Hadi, 2 daughters named Nilufa Begum and Jenifa Begum as his legal heirs and they inherited the deceased Md Nurul Hadi's 420 decimals of land out of which the defendant got 63 and 3/4 decimals, son Md Ajmal Hadi got 120 and 1/8 decimals and each daughter got 111 and 9/16 decimals. As the defendant living in United Kingdom she executed a power of attorney being its No. 4078 dated 7-12-2008 in favour of his brother plaintiff No. 1 and one relative plaintiff No.2 to look after her 210 decimals of land. She did not obtain any power of attorney from her son and daughters to sell any property and she never intended to sell any of her or her son and daughters property to anybody. When the defendant came to know that the plaintiffs are trying to grab her property she came back to Bangladesh and cancelled the said power of attorney by executing registered power of attorney cancellation deed being No. 2672 dated 18-8-2009 and also on 7-9-2009 the defendant published a notice in Shaptahik Jatiya Barta in respect of said cancellation of power of attorney although the plaintiffs entered into a so called unregistered baina deed with one Md Yakub Nobi and Md Sheikh Farid on 5-7-2009 in respect of the defendant's land. In this background, Md Yakub Nobi and Md Sheikh Farid filed a title suit being title suit No. 34 of 2009 for specific performance of contract against the plaintiffs of the instant case and the defendant MosammatNazma Begum of the instant case was not being made defendant in that suit. The said Md Yakub Nobi and Md Sheikh Farid made a solenama and on the basis of the said solenama Md Yakub Nobi and Md Sheikh Farid obtained a sole decree and on getting information about the said title suit No. 34 of 2009 as well as decree, the defendant of the instant suit filed civil suit No.4 of 2010 praying a decree declaring that the decree passed in title suit No. 34 of 2009 is illegal and void and the said suit is now pending for hearing. The defendant opposite party neither executed the alleged bainanama nor took any part of the consideration money amounting to Taka 10,00,000 or any money as consideration whatsoever. Further, the land of the defendant was not mortgaged to anybody and therefore, the alleged payment of Taka 5,00,000 to the mortgagee by the plaintiffs are false and without any legal basis. The plaintiffs brought the suit with intent to illegally grab the defendant's property and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
